about: What the dashboard (web) and the phone app (phone) each do with Nevela's API. Every route under auth/ and _nevela/, and each resource route that isn't plain create-read-update-delete, is listed: "both", or one of web, phone, none or linked with the reason the other side has none. linked: reached by an address the API hands back, not one either app builds. A new route can't ship without its line (apps/api/tests/Feature/ParityTest.php), and each claim is checked against the apps' code (scripts/parity.test.mjs). The docs page is apps/docs/src/content/docs/reference/web-and-phone.md.

POST auth/magic-link.web: A sign-in link opens a dashboard page. The phone signs in with an emailed code instead, which works with a dashboard or without one.

POST auth/magic-link/verify.web: The other half of the sign-in link.

POST auth/passkey/options.web: Signing in to a phone app with a passkey needs a build tied to the app's own domain, which an app run in Expo Go isn't.

POST auth/passkey.web: The other half of signing in with a passkey.

GET auth/oauth/{provider}/app.linked: Where Google or GitHub sends the phone's browser back to, which hands it to the app.

POST auth/confirm/passkey/options.web: Confirming with a passkey needs a build of the phone app tied to the app's own domain. The phone confirms with the password, an emailed code or the authenticator app.

POST auth/passkeys/options.web: Adding a passkey on the phone needs a build tied to the app's own domain. The phone lists and removes them.

POST auth/passkeys.web: The other half of adding a passkey.

PATCH auth/passkeys/{id}.none: Renaming a passkey: in the API for an app's own screens. Each passkey is named when it is added.

GET _nevela/ping.none: For `nevela status` and the like, to tell a Nevela API from another program on the same port.

GET public/_nevela/resources.phone: What a visitor may browse before signing in, such as a shop's products. The dashboard's public pages are generated from the same descriptions.

GET _nevela/files/{path}.linked: A stored file, at the address each record carries.

GET _nevela/private-link/{slug}/{id}/{fi.linked: A private file by a link that works for a few minutes, which the phone opens in its browser.

GET _nevela/private/{slug}/{id}/{field}.web: A private file, fetched with the token. The phone's browser can't send it, so the phone asks for a link instead.

POST _nevela/private/{slug}/{id}/{field}.phone: The dashboard's server fetches a private file with the token for the browser, so it needs no link.

GET _nevela/profiles.none: Which picture sizes exist, for an app's own code. Each picture already carries its sizes.

GET _nevela/resources.phone: The dashboard is generated from the resources' descriptions, so it has them built in. The phone reads them when it starts.

GET _nevela/forms/{slug}.web: What a public form checks and has turned away. Public forms belong to the dashboard's public site, which the phone has no part in.

GET _nevela/openapi.json.web: The API page, for developers at a desk.

PUT _nevela/push-tokens.phone: Push notifications go to phones. The dashboard has the bell.

DELETE _nevela/push-tokens/{token}.phone: The other half of push notifications.

GET _nevela/trash/_status.web: Whether the dashboard's menu shows Trash. The phone shows it to anyone who may delete something.

POST {slug}/_bulk.web: The "Add several" grid: typing many records in rows at once wants a keyboard and a wide screen.

file.partly: The phone opens every file, and takes pictures from its camera or library. Attaching any other file, such as a PDF, is the dashboard's for now.

json.web: Edited as JSON, which wants a keyboard and room to see it. The phone shows it and leaves it as it is.
